# IRGC says forces 'finger on trigger,' vows devastating response to US, Israel



Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said on Monday the country’s armed forces were “finger on the trigger” and ready to deliver “decisive and devastating” responses to the United States and Israel amid heightened threats of further military escalation.

In a statement marking the anniversary of the start of the 1980s Iran-Iraq war, the IRGC said Iran’s forces had reached a level of military capability that allowed them to neutralize threats “at their source,” citing what it described as the achievements of recent military operations against the US and Israel.

The Guards also pointed to Iran’s handling of the Strait of Hormuz as evidence of its military power and said Washington and Israel would eventually have to accept a region without their presence.

# Don’t Ask How This War Ends

It is, unfortunately, the wrong question.

By [Eliot A. Cohen](https://www.theatlantic.com/author/eliot-a-cohen/)

Contributor / Getty

During the 2003 Iraq War, then–Major General David Petraeus famously said to the journalist and historian Rick Atkinson, “Tell me how this ends.” It is the obvious query to be posed about the conflict with Iran, but it requires a different answer.

In the middle of a war, few people are inclined to take the longest view of its origins. The implications of the Austro-Hungarian annexation of Bosnia Herzegovina, in 1908, were probably of little interest to Marshal Ferdinand Foch, Field Marshal Douglas Haig, or General John J. Pershing in 1917. But the questions of when and why a war began are essential to understanding it.

In the case of the Iran war, we must see the conflict not as a war unto itself but rather as the latest campaign in a war that has gone on since the 1979 Iranian revolution, conducted for the most part with covert warfare, naval skirmishes, and raids. The launch of Operation Midnight Hammer in 2025, in which the U.S. targeted Iranian nuclear facilities, marked a new phase. The war has been fought by the United States, Israel, and most of the Persian Gulf’s Sunni monarchies against a regime that combines an unappeasable anti-Western ideology and exterminationist hatred of Israel with a desire to assert old Persian imperial reach.

# As Trump and Xi Meet, the U.S. and China Are ‘Shin-Kicking Under the Table.’

Beyond warm meetings between their leaders, the countries are engaging in tit-for-tat measures that call into question the stability of their arrangement.

When the United States and China reached a trade truce during a meeting in South Korea a year ago, it helped restore some stability to an economic relationship that was threatening to spin out of control.

The agreement forced President Trump to walk back punishing tariffs on Chinese exports, and made China promise to maintain exports of critical minerals that it had cut off in response to the president’s levies.

Negotiators appear to be preparing to extend that agreement as Xi Jinping, the leader of China, comes to Washington to meet with Mr. Trump later this week. On Sunday night, U.S. officials said that they would discuss setting up a dialogue on artificial intelligence and promoting trade in nonsensitive goods like energy and consumer products when Mr. Trump meets Mr. Xi this week.

But despite the plans for a warm state dinner and other pomp and circumstance at the White House, the truce between the United States and China has been uneasier than it might appear. It has not prevented either government from continuing to take action against one another in ways that have sometimes threatened to upset the agreement entirely. Both nations have blamed each other for violating promises made last October in Korea.
